vulnerabilities.description: No validation on customer name input. Users can submit very long strings or special characters that could cause database bloat or display issues.
No validation on WhatsApp input. Should enforce numeric-only format and reasonable length (e.g., 4-8 digits for Panama phone numbers).
Uses unsafe_allow_html=True with user-controlled link_wa variable. While URL-encoded by quote(), using unsafe_allow_html is discouraged. Could be exploited if quote() has unexpected behavior.

Uses execSync() with shell string instead of execFileSync() with array arguments. While the command is hardcoded, it violates defense-in-depth principle established in the codebase (see lines 89, 92).
Uses execSync() with shell string containing pipes and grep commands. Not following execFileSync best practice used elsewhere in codebase.
Uses execSync() with shell string for process inspection. Should use execFileSync() with array arguments.
json.loads() called without prior validation. Could throw exception if items field is corrupted, though it's server-side only.
No authentication or authorization mechanism. Any user with network access can view all quotations, customer names, and phone numbers without restrictions.

recommendations: Add input validation to customer name (string length limit, alphanumeric + spaces only)
Add input validation to WhatsApp field (numeric only, length 4-8 digits for Panama numbers)
Replace unsafe_allow_html=True with safe HTML escaping or use Streamlit's built-in link button component
Refactor statusline.js to use execFileSync('ps', ['aux'], ...) instead of execSync with shell strings
Add try-catch around json.loads() in database.py with proper error logging
Implement basic authentication (login page) to protect customer data access
Add database query logging for audit trail of who accessed what quotations
Set reasonable length limits on text inputs (e.g., 100 chars for name, 8 for WhatsApp)
Consider encrypting WhatsApp numbers in database if they're considered sensitive
Add CSRF protection if Streamlit app is deployed on internet-facing server
